findings.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source of this compilation, including diagnostics with Location.None. Existing diagnostics created with null/no location (e.g. MsgPack003/004/005 or other type-level diagnostics where GetIdentifierLocation returns null) were previously reported and now are silently dropped, so users no longer see warnings or errors they saw before. This is a behavior change broader than the metadata-symbol crash.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005/etc.) and add a case where the diagnostic location is Location.None or comes from a partial or generated syntax tree. Assert the diagnostic is still reported on head as on base. A failing test shows the regression.

findings.claim: The new early return for any generic type whose OriginalDefinition has no declaring syntax skips all further collection, including generic types from referenced assemblies that previously got a closed-generic formatter registered. A referenced-assembly generic struct without its own resolver, or one that is not a [MessagePackObject], previously went through CollectGeneric and now yields no formatter entry in the generated resolver. This changes generated output users snapshot, and could cause runtime formatter-not-found errors. It also applies to BCL generics such as ValueTuple<,> or KeyValuePair<,> if they reach this point.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests. Add a sample with a member of type ValueTuple<int,string> or KeyValuePair<,> and a closed generic from a referenced assembly. Compare generated resolver output on base and head for missing GetFormatter entries.

findings.claim: The guard sits after the custom-formatter and enum checks but the diff context does not show whether it also precedes the handling of built-in generic collections (List<T>, Dictionary<,>, Nullable<T>), which are metadata symbols. If it does, those generic members are skipped, and their type arguments are no longer collected, so user types nested inside them lose generated formatters.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate for a [MessagePackObject] with List<MyType> and Nullable<MyStruct> members, on base and head. Diff the output to confirm MyType's formatter is still registered.
